comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (GAP 3) — analytic core.** Prove $T_\psi^*\mu\ll\mu$ with density $R_\psi$, i.e.

$$\int F(u-\psi)\,d\mu(u)=\int F(u)\,R_\psi(u)\,d\mu(u)$$

for a separating class of bounded measurable functionals $F$.

**Why hardest.** In $d=3$ the renormalization is **not a pure shift**: the formal computation $V(u-\psi)-V(u)$ involves Wick powers whose counterterms must transform covariantly under $u\mapsto u-\psi$. One must prove that no anomalous renormalization-induced Jacobian appears beyond the explicit Wick terms in $R_\psi$ — a genuine risk of a hidden divergence. Two routes, each needing its own justification:

1. **Stochastic-quantization + Girsanov.** Use a stationary solution of the $\Phi^4_3$ SPDE; the shifted field $u-\psi$ solves an SPDE with renormalized drift $:(u-\psi)^3:\,-\,:\!u^3\!:$; apply Girsanov on $C([0,T];C^{-1/2-\kappa})$ and verify a Novikov-type / uniform-integrability condition on the renormalized drift difference.
2. **Boué–Dupuis variational (Barashkov–Gubinelli).** Use $-\log\int e^{-F}d\mu=\inf_v\mathbb{E}[F(W+I(v))+\tfrac12\int|v|^2]$, encode the shift in the drift, and identify the free-energy difference with $\log R_\psi$.

**Deliverable.** A fully justified derivation of the identity with explicit control of the renormalized nonlinear functionals and an argument that the counterterms are shift-covariant up to finite, computable corrections already contained in $R_\psi$.
